source_text: Ἴδωμεν δὲ εἰ οὗτος ὁ λαὸς κληρονομεῖ ἡ ὁ πρῶτος, καὶ εἰ ἡ διαθήκη εἰς ἡμᾶς ἢ εἰς ἐκείνους. ἀκούσατε οὖν περὶ τοῦ λαοῦ τί λέγει ἡ γραφή: Ἐδεῖτο δὲ Ἰσαὰκ περὶ Ῥεβέκκας τῆς γυναικὸς αὐτοῦ, ὅτι στεῖρα ἦν: καὶ συνέλαβεν. εἶτα ἐξῆλθεν Ῥεβέκκα πυθέσθαι παρὰ κυρίου, καὶ εἶπεν κύριος πρὸς αὐτήν: Δύο ἔθνη ἐν τῇ γαστρί σου καὶ δύο λαοὶ ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ σου, καὶ ὑπερέξει λαὸς λαοῦ καὶ ὁ μείζων δουλεύσει τῷ ἐλάσσονι. αἰσθάνεσθαι ὀφείλετε, τίς ὁ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ τίς ἡ Ῥεβέκκα. καὶ ἐπὶ τίνων δέδειχεν, ὅτι μείζων ὁ λαὸς οὗτος ἢ ἐκεῖνος. καὶ ἐν ἄλλῃ προφητείᾳ λέγει φανερώτερον ὁ Ἰακὼβ πρὸς Ἰωσὴφ τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ, λέγων: Ἰδού, οὐκ ἐστέρησέν με κύριος τοῦ προσώπου σου: προσάγαγέ μοι τοὺς υἱούς σου, ἵνα εὐλογήσω αὐτούς. καὶ προσήγαγεν Ἐφραὶμ καὶ Μανασσῆ, τὸν Μανασσῆ θέλων ἵνα εὐλογηθῇ, ὅτι πρεσβύτερος ἦν: ὁ γὰρ Ἰωσὴφ προσήγαγεν εἰς τὴν δεξιὰν χεῖρα τοῦ πατρὸς Ἰακώβ. εἶδεν δὲ Ἰακὼβ τύπον τῷ πνεύματι τοῦ λαοῦ τοῦ μεταξύ: καὶ τί λέγει; Καὶ ἐποίησεν Ἰακὼβ ἐναλλὰξ τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐπέθηκεν τὴν δεξιὰν ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἐφραίμ, τοῦ δευτέρου καὶ νεωτέρου, καὶ εὐλόγησεν αὐτόν. καὶ εἶπεν Ἰωσὴφ πρὸς Ἰακώβ: Μετάθες σου τὴν δεξιὰν ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν Μανασσῆ, ὅτι πρωτότοκός μου υἱός ἐστιν. καὶ εἶπεν Ἰακὼβ πρὸς Ἰωσήφ: Οἰδα, τέκνον, οἶδα: ἀλλ’ ὁ μείζων δουλεύσει τῷ ἐλάσσονι, καὶ οὗτος δὲ εὐλογηθήσεται. βλέπετε, ἐπὶ τίνων τέθεικεν, τὸν λαὸν τοῦτον εἶναι πρῶτον καὶ τῆς διαθήκης κληρονόμον. εἰ οὖν ἔτι καὶ διὰ τοῦ Ἀβραὰμ ἐμνήσθη, ἀπέχομεν τὸ τέλειον τῆς γνώσεως ἡμῶν. τί οὖν λέγει τῷ Ἀβραάμ, ὅτε μόνος πιστεύσας ἐτέθη εἰς δικαιοσύνην; Ἰδού, τέθεικά σε, Ἀβραάμ, πατέρα ἐθνῶν τῶν πιστευόντων δἰ ἀκροβυστίας τῷ θεῷ.
pass_a_gloss: Let us see if this people inherits or the first one, and if the covenant is to us or to them. Therefore, hear regarding the people what the scripture says: And Isaac entreated regarding Rebekka his wife, because she was barren: and she conceived. Then Rebekka went to inquire of the Lord, and the Lord said to her: Two nations are in your womb and two peoples in your belly, and one people will excel over the other people and the greater will serve the lesser. You ought to understand, who Isaac is and who Rebekka is. And regarding whom did He show that this people is greater than that one. And in another prophecy Jacob says more clearly to Joseph his son, saying: Behold, the Lord has not deprived me of your face: bring me your sons, so that I may bless them. And he brought Ephraim and Manasseh, wanting Manasseh to be blessed, because he was older: for Joseph brought him to the right hand of his father Jacob. And Jacob saw a type by the Spirit of the people in between: and what does he say? And Jacob crossed his hands and put his right hand on the head of Ephraim, the second and younger, and blessed him. And Joseph said to Jacob: Transfer your right hand to the head of Manasseh, because he is my firstborn son. And Jacob said to Joseph: I know, child, I know: but the greater will serve the lesser, and this one also will be blessed. See, regarding whom did He establish this people to be first and heir of the covenant. If then He still remembered through Abraham, we possess the fullness of our knowledge. What then does He say to Abraham, when being alone he was reckoned as righteous? Behold, I have made you, Abraham, father of nations of those who believe through uncircumcision to God.

pass_b_english: Let us find out whether this people or the first one inherits the promises, and whether the covenant belongs to us or to them. Listen, then, to what Scripture says about this people: Isaac prayed for his wife Rebekah because she was barren, and she conceived (Gen 25:21). Later Rebekah went to inquire of the Lord, and the Lord told her, "Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples will be separated from within you; one people will be stronger than the other, and the older will serve the younger" (Gen 25:23). You must understand who Isaac and Rebekah represent, and concerning whom God showed that this people is greater than the other. In another prophecy Jacob speaks even more clearly to his son Joseph: "Look, the Lord has not deprived me of seeing your face; bring me your sons so that I may bless them" (Gen 48:11). So Joseph brought Ephraim and Manasseh, wanting Manasseh to receive the blessing because he was the firstborn; he placed Manasseh at Jacob's right hand. But Jacob, seeing a type by the Spirit of the people to come, crossed his hands and laid his right hand on the head of Ephraim, the younger, and blessed him (Gen 48:13-14). When Joseph objected, saying, "Move your right hand to Manasseh's head, for he is my firstborn," Jacob replied, "I know, my son, I know; yet the greater shall serve the lesser, and this one also shall be blessed" (Gen 48:17-19). See, then, concerning whom God established this people as first and heir of the covenant. If He still remembered the promise through Abraham, we possess the fullness of our knowledge. What does He say to Abraham when, believing alone, he was counted as righteous? "Behold, I have made you, Abraham, a father of many nations of those who believe through uncircumcision toward God" (Gen 17:5; Rom 4:11).

review.notes: Pass B adds significant content not present in the Greek source, specifically interpreting the text with biblical citations and expanding the meaning of phrases. For example, the Greek 'δύο ἔθνη ἐν τῇ γαστρί σου καὶ δύο λαοὶ ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ σου' (Two nations are in your womb and two peoples in your belly) is rendered in Pass B as 'Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples will be separated from within you' (Gen 25:23), adding the clause 'will be separated from within you' which is not in the Greek. Furthermore, Pass B adds 'When Joseph objected, saying...' to introduce the dialogue, whereas the Greek simply states 'And Joseph said to Jacob...' (καὶ εἶπεν Ἰωσὴφ πρὸς Ἰακώβ). Pass B also adds 'the promise' in 'If He still remembered the promise through Abraham', whereas the Greek 'διὰ τοῦ Ἀβραὰμ' does not contain the noun 'promise'.
reasons: Pass B adds content not found in the Greek source: 'will be separated from within you' (Gen 25:23) and 'When Joseph objected, saying...' (to introduce 'καὶ εἶπεν Ἰωσὴφ πρὸς Ἰακώβ'). Pass B also adds 'the promise' to 'If He still remembered through Abraham' (εἰ οὖν ἔτι καὶ διὰ τοῦ Ἀβραὰμ ἐμνήσθη).
